prepare: RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.89.0 cargo tree --locked -p base16ct -e normal,build,dev --features alloc > /dev/null
proposal.note: Unit: base16ct, the workspace's top-ranked crate. It is a constant-time hex encoder and decoder with no dependencies, 381 lines of scalar code that never branches on the data, and 11 integration tests of its own. Every command uses -p base16ct --features alloc, because one of the tests and the *_vec / encode_string functions need that feature. There are three cachegrind instruction-count metrics, each with an --inputs-only fixed command. encode_ir covers lower/upper encode, encode_str and encode_string. decode_ir covers lower/upper/mixed decode, including inputs with a bad character, plus decode_vec. display_ir covers HexDisplay in the {}, {:x} and {:X} formats, which currently writes the output one byte at a time through the formatter. The inputs are seeded and sized like digests and keys (16 to 64 bytes) or like messages (up to 4 KiB). In the trial, calibration took 12 s, run-to-run variation was 0 and the equivalence digests were identical. The work outside the library is 23%, 35% and 7% of the three counts. The equivalence harness prints the output of every public function for: all byte values, every pair of characters, odd lengths, invalid characters, output buffers that are too short or too long, Display/Debug text including padding, and the error texts. Patches may only change base16ct/src/**.
